minutes.headline: Select Board suspended Mickey Shays' liquor license for two days after finding false renewals and no manager notice.
minutes.summary: The board held a hearing on the Mickey Shays license, whose listed manager had left in 2010, and found violations. It set a two-day suspension on a split vote. Members also appointed three Council on Aging members, replaced two public weighers, renewed earth removal permits, and heard the town manager on road work and a Leominster casino proposal. A board member raised concern about the town clerk's election food payments.

public_comment.topic: A resident raised concern about Highland Street traffic, a conflict of interest in PJ Keating employees serving as public weighers, and whether earth removal licenses were issued to a deceased person or the correct entity.

what_happened.line: The Select Board found that the Mickey Shays liquor license holder failed to notify the town of a manager change and filed false renewal applications for 2010, 2011 and 2012.
The board imposed a two-day suspension of the BNH Corporation license, to be served on a Friday and Saturday in October.
The suspension dates were set for about the 18th and 19th of October, with a letter to follow from town counsel.
The board approved all earth removal permit renewals as identified by the town manager, and will hold a workshop on the earth removal bylaw and closure plans.
The board approved three Council on Aging nominations and two public weigher appointments at PJ Keating.

why_it_matters: Liquor license renewals are filed under oath, and the hearing shows the board treating inaccurate renewal filings and unreported manager changes as grounds for a suspension of a local business's license.
Earth removal permits govern gravel and soil operations and their truck traffic, and the planned workshop could change the bylaw and the closure plans that apply to those sites.
watch_next: The suspension dates of about the 18th and 19th of October, and the letter from town counsel.
The board workshop on the earth removal bylaw and closure plans, and the circulated sewer commission Fitchburg agreement.
